title: ‘PNP remains impartial, gives equal protection’
summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) assured the public of its impartiality amid a string of criticisms from Vice President Sara Duterte that it is being used as an “enforcement arm” of…

blocks.text: More than 300 newly appointed police non-commissioned officers from the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) arrive at the Manila Police District on January 26, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) assured the public of its impartiality amid a string of criticisms from Vice President Sara Duterte that it is being used as an “enforcement arm” of politicians.

Claiming that she does not feel safe in this country, Duterte blasted the PNP, particularly its chief, Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., after he refuted her camp’s story that a former household staffer and four other people were allegedly held captive unless they signed an affidavit containing false allegations against the Vice President.
In a statement yesterday, Nartatez shrugged off claims of political bias.

“Impartiality is a principle that we strive to uphold in every police operation and public service,” the country’s top cop said. “Our commitment is to treat everyone with fairness, respect and compassion, while providing equal protection under the law regardless of one’s position or political affiliation.”'
Police’s “no rescue” remark triggered the Vice President’s outburst on Saturday.
Nartatez said it was important for him to respond to these reports with “factual narration of what really transpired.”

Meanwhile, Malacañang yesterday labeled Duterte’s claims of feeling threatened as fabricated, suggesting instead that she may actually be afraid of taking the witness stand in her ongoing impeachment trial.
Palace press officer Claire Castro called Duterte’s remarks “kwento-kwento lang” and challenged her to refute financial records submitted against her in the Senate proceedings.

“Can she handle testifying and refuting the reports and records of the banks, AMLC (Anti-Money Laundering Council) and BIR (Bureau of Internal Revenue)? That’s what everybody is waiting for. So don’t be afraid if truth is on your side,” Castro said. — Neil Jayson Servallos
